purpose: Lomustine is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat certain types of brain tumors and Hodgkin's lymphoma (a type of cancer that affects the lymph system). It is often used when other treatments have not worked well enough. Your doctor may also use it for other cancers depending on your situation.
how_it_works: Lomustine works by attaching to and damaging the DNA inside cancer cells, which stops them from growing and multiplying. Think of it like putting a wrench in the machinery that cancer cells need to copy themselves. Because it can cross into the brain, it is especially useful for brain tumors.
common_side_effects: Nausea and vomiting (usually within a few hours of taking it), loss of appetite, mouth sores, hair thinning, fatigue, and low blood cell counts (which can increase your risk of infection, bleeding, or anemia). Nausea often improves after the first day.
warnings: This medicine can seriously lower your blood counts, so your doctor will check your blood regularly — usually every 6 weeks. It is taken only ONCE every 6 weeks, not daily, so it is very important not to take extra doses as this can be life-threatening. It can harm an unborn baby, so use reliable birth control. Tell your doctor right away if you develop fever, unusual bruising or bleeding, or trouble breathing.
typical_dosing: Lomustine is taken by mouth as a capsule, usually as a single dose once every 6 weeks. The exact dose depends on your body size and overall health. It is often taken on an empty stomach or with a light meal to reduce nausea. Your doctor will tell you exactly how many capsules to take and when.
